summary: Cross-model embedding format incompatibility causing rerank queue buildup and degraded latency
description:
Issue summary: Customer ClearSight reports that calls to the /v1/rerank endpoint started experiencing long tail latency and queueing beginning 2026-03-10 08:30 UTC. The rerank results also show quality regressions (unexpected ordering) when the customer mixes vectors produced by two different embedding variants in the same request.

Impact: Intermittent timeouts from the customer's service (503/504), increased 95th/99th percentile latency for rerank API in us-west, and customer-facing throughput drops. Several high-volume requests queued, causing rate-limit-like behavior and triggering their dedicated capacity autoscale.

Environment: Dedicated tenant (ClearSight) on prod:us-west using a mix of embed-lite-v2 (512 dims, L2-normalized) and embed-highdim-2025 (1024 dims, raw float) produced by their pipeline. Rerank service is expected to accept homogeneous vectors but did not validate dims in upstream request layer.

Steps to reproduce:
- Construct two embedding arrays: one from embed-lite-v2 (shape N x 512, l2-normalized) and one from embed-highdim-2025 (shape N x 1024, raw).
- Send a single /v1/rerank request containing a candidate list where some candidates include 512-d vectors and others include 1024-d vectors (no explicit embedding_version header).
- Observe immediate enqueuing and a sharp latency increase for that request ID (~>5s p99), occasionally resulting in 503 or rerank returning lower-quality ordering.

Observed logs: Trace IDs: rnk-20260310-8a4f, rnk-20260310-8b11. Error snippets show the rerank evaluator logging "embedding dim mismatch - implicit upcast" and downstream trace showing fallback to CPU quant path. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rerank/us-west?panelId=7&from=2026-03-10T08:00:00Z&to=2026-03-10T09:00:00Z. Slack thread: #support (thread ts 1700003000.002200).
steps_to_reproduce: Combine both types in a single /v1/rerank request payload without embedding_version headers
Send to customer's dedicated endpoint in us-west and observe latency and ordering
logs: 2026-03-10T08:34:12Z rnk-20260310-8a4f rerank WARN embedding dim mismatch - implicit upcast
2026-03-10T08:34:13Z rnk-20260310-8a4f rerank INFO fallback to cpu-quant path, estimated token cost +1.9x
2026-03-10T08:34:14Z api-gateway 429 upstream queue depth exceeded for tenant clearsight
comments: 2026-03-10 09:02 - Ava Martinez (Support): Acknowledged customer report, requested sample payload and trace IDs. Asked for exact model variants and whether any normalization was applied client-side.

2026-03-10 09:20 - Customer (ClearSight - S. Patel): Provided sample payloads and confirmed the two models above; they said their ingestion pipeline accidentally stitched outputs during a rollout and didn't set embedding_version headers.

2026-03-10 11:05 - Ravi Shah (SRE): Observed sharp p99 increase aligned with trace IDs; rerank service allowed mixed-dim vectors and triggered a slow conversion in the scoring path. Filed INT-4012 to track an internal validation fix.

2026-03-11 07:18 - Eng (L. Chen): Root cause identified: upstream request validator omitted embedding dimension validation when a mixed candidate list is present. Implicit handling attempted to upcast 512->1024 and call into CPU fallback for several heavy kernels, causing latency spike. Created PR #1287 to add strict validation + syntactic hinting for embedding_version header.

2026-03-11 14:30 - Support (A. Martinez): Communicated temporary workaround to customer: ensure homogeneous embedding dims per request or include embedding_version header; If mixing is unavoidable, pad 512-d vectors with zeros to match 1024 length as a short-term mitigation.

2026-03-12 03:05 - Ravi Shah (SRE): Hotfix deployed to prod: validator now rejects mixed-dim requests with clear 400 response and guidance. Gradual rollout completed across us-west. Monitoring shows p99 latency back to baseline.
2026-03-12 10:00 - Customer (S. Patel): Confirmed issue resolved from their perspective; no further timeouts observed in last 24h and quality returned to expected ordering.
investigation_notes: Checked Grafana: rerank queue depth spiked at 08:34 UTC, correlated with increase in cpu pathway calls (serving-runtime cpu_binder).
Heap/CPU profiles captured for one trace showed expensive memcpy and zero-padding steps executed under request lock while scoring ran on CPU vector kernels.

Hypothesis: absence of embedding_version header + mixing dims caused system to try compatibility conversion; conversion fallback path is not gated by timeout and increased latency drastically under concurrency.
Confirmed that prior safety check for vector length exists at model-serving layer but the rerank preprocessor path bypassed it during a historical refactor (see commit 6a2f8b3).
Related PR adding strict dims check and clear error messages: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rerank-service/pull/1287
Related internal ticket: INT-4012 for adding e2e tests and SDK validation helpers.
resolution_notes: Deployed a validator that rejects mixed-dimension embedding lists with an informative 400 response explaining expected dims and embedding_version header format. Back-ported a short-circuit to avoid implicit upcast/conversion on hot paths. Created SDK guidance and sample code for ClearSight and added an integration test asserting consistent dims. Customer confirmed resolution. Action items: (1) Add automatic recommend-converter utility for customers who need cross-model compatibility; (2) Add telemetry to count mixed-dim attempts and trigger early alerts; (3) Update runbook with exact error messages and workaround steps.
postmortem_followup: Create conversion utility RFC (owner: L. Chen)
Add mixed-dim detector alert to PagerDuty playbook (owner: Ravi Shah)
Ship SDK helper that fails fast with clear error for mixed dims (owner: Developer Experience)
public_communication: Customer-facing note provided: 'We temporarily observed elevated rerank latencies when mixing embeddings from different model families. The service now returns a clear error for mixed-dimension requests and we provided migration steps. We apologize for the disruption and are working on an automated converter for mixed workloads.'
